summary: Look up each symbol's value in a dict. If a symbol is smaller than the one after it (like the I in IV), subtract it; otherwise add it. This one look-ahead rule covers all six subtractive pairs (T3 — string processing with a dict).

blocks.title: Read the numeral
blocks.text: `.strip()` removes stray spaces and `.upper()` accepts lowercase input, so every character is a key in the dict.

blocks.title: Symbol values
blocks.text: A dict maps each symbol to its value in O(1).

blocks.title: Walk through the symbols
blocks.text: We loop by index because we need to peek at the NEXT symbol.

blocks.title: Smaller before bigger → subtract
blocks.text: `i + 1 < len(s)` is checked first: the last symbol has no next one, and `s[i + 1]` would crash. In `IX`, I (1) is before X (10), so we subtract 1 and later add 10 → 9.

blocks.title: Otherwise add
blocks.text: Normal case: the symbol's value is added.

complexity: Time O(L) with L ≤ 15 symbols — instant.
pitfalls: Hard-coding the pairs with `replace` and missing one.
